newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa rebounds to end up on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa rebounds to end up on shortcovering.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures rebounded from more than five-month lows to end up sharply Friday on speculative short covering, traders said.
"When the market held support, it forced the specs to cover shorts," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast.
Chart-driven trade and speculative selling drove the benchmark December contract to a low of $1,329 a tonne, where the contract found firm chart support, dealers said.
Benchmark December cocoa settled up $18 a tonne, at $1,373, after ranging between $1,379 and $1,329. March rose $18 to $1,407, while the rest ended $10 to $21 higher.
Dealers said the market trailed London, where LCE cocoa futures reversed to end sharply higher after sinking to fresh six-month lows Friday amid talk of a private crop estimate.
New York traders said the estimate by trade house Cargill pegged the world 1996/97 cocoa supply deficit at 178,000 tonnes, down from its forecast in June of 185,000 tonnes.

Cargill reportedly revised upward the 1995/96 world cocoa surplus to 126,000 tonnes from its earlier forecast of 65,000 and put the Ivorian 1996/97 crop at 850,000 tonnes, Ghanaian 275,000 and Indonesian 330,000.
Cargill sources in the U.S. declined to confirm the data.
Prendergast said although the revisions were not necessarily bullish the reminder of a sizable world supply deficit was probably enough to spark buying after recent price declines.
December cocoa has fallen from a two-month high at $1,443 on August 21.

Technically, traders termed December's Friday trading action, with the contract trading below its low on Thursday but ending above Thursday's high, was bullish. They pegged December's near-term resistance at $1,390 and also $1,405.
Volume was active at an estimated 12,185 lots.
